extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in algebraic geometry (learning/teaching Serre duality)
extracted.subtask_short: proving Serre duality for projective schemes
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition and proof-plan for Serre duality in several variants (vector bundles, Hom, Ext) on projective k-schemes, including precise desiderata, definitions (dualizing sheaf and trace), key reductions (to projective space via finite maps), and the hypotheses (Cohen–Macaulay, flatness) needed for each version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determinant of the cotangent bundle as dualizing for smooth varieties (Desideratum 30.1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is smooth, we want ωX = KX (recall KX = det ΩX) — the miracle that the canonical bundle is Serre-dualizing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In particular, ωX should be an invertible sheaf. The text notes this is harder to prove than the basic duality statements and will be obtained later (Exercise 30.4.I); also ωX is invertible if X is a regular embedding in a smooth variety (Exercise 30.4.H).

rubrics_metrics.name: Functorial Serre duality for vector bundles (Desideratum 30.1.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For F locally free of finite rank on an n-dimensional projective k-scheme X, construct a functorial isomorphism Hi(X,F) ∼= H^{n−i}(X, F^∨ ⊗ ωX)^∨ (equation (30.1.2.1)), equivalently a perfect pairing functorial in F (30.1.2.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One should construct a specific isomorphism (or perfect pairing) functorial in F. The trace version is obtained via a cup product Hi(X,F) × H^{n−i}(X,F^∨ ⊗ ωX) → H^n(X,ωX) followed by the trace map t: H^n(X,ωX) → k. The text states this holds when X is Cohen–Macaulay (hence when smooth) and indicates the functorial version will be proved (Corollary 30.3.10) and the trace version indicated (Remark 30.3.15).

rubrics_metrics.name: Functorial Serre duality for Hom (Desideratum 30.1.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any coherent sheaf F on a pure n-dimensional projective k-scheme X, there is a functorial isomorphism Hom(F,ωX) ∼= H^n(X,F)^∨ (equation (30.1.3.1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a natural candidate pairing Hom(F,ωX) × H^n(X,F) → H^n(X,ωX) and composition with a trace linear functional t on H^n(X,ωX) should give a perfect pairing (trace version). Functoriality in F means the isomorphism is a natural transformation of functors in F. Exercise 30.1.A shows functorial and trace versions are equivalent in this case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of dualizing sheaf and trace (Definition 30.1.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: A coherent sheaf ωX together with a map t: H^n(X,ωX) → k is called dualizing if for all coherent sheaves F the natural map Hom(F,ωX) × H^n(X,F) → H^n(X,ωX) →^t k is a perfect pairing (equation (30.1.4.1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such (ωX,t) exists we say X satisfies Serre duality (for Hom). This is the formal criterion one should check when asserting Serre duality for a scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness of dualizing sheaf and trace (Proposition 30.1.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a dualizing sheaf and trace (ωX,t) exists for X, this data is unique up to unique isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: functorial bijections Hom(F,ωX) ∼= H^n(X,F)^∨ ∼= Hom(F,ω'_X) for all F induce a unique isomorphism ωX ∼= ω'_X and the traces agree under this isomorphism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projective-space dualizing sheaf and check for line bundles (30.1.6, 30.1.B, 30.1.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: For P^n_k define ω_{P^n} = O(-n-1); choose an isomorphism H^n(P^n_k, ω_{P^n}) ∼= k. For F = O(m) the natural map (30.1.4.1) is a perfect pairing; hence for direct sums of line bundles it is perfect, and then extend to all coherent sheaves (Proposition 30.1.7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises 30.1.B and subsequent argument via resolutions (Theorem 15.3.1) and the five-lemma give the projective-space case, which is the key base case for reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functorial/trace Serre duality for Ext (Desideratum 30.1.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension: for all i there is an isomorphism Ext^i(·, ωX) ∼= H^{n−i}(X, ·)^∨ (equation (30.1.9.1)); this is the functorial Serre duality for Ext. The trace version is obtained from a Yoneda cup product Ext^i(F,ωX) × H^{n−i}(X,F) → H^n(X,ωX) followed by t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This stronger statement implies the vector-bundle version (Exercise 30.2.I). The trace-version involves defining the cup product on Ext; the text proves the functorial version for Cohen–Macaulay schemes in Corollary 30.3.14, and proves the projective-space case first (30.1.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Projective-space case for Ext (30.1.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Functorial Serre duality for Ext holds for projective space P^n_k; Ext^i_{P^n}(·, ω_{P^n}) is a (contravariant) universal δ-functor and is identified with (H^{n−i}(P^n,·))^∨.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the universal δ-functor criterion (Definition 23.2.7, Theorem 23.2.8) and the fact Ext^0 matches H^n(·)^∨; Exercises 30.1.C and 30.1.D guide the verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of Cohen–Macaulay hypotheses (30.1.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cohen–Macaulay hypotheses are necessary for the stronger duality statements; counterexamples exist (e.g., X the union of two 2-planes in P^4 meeting at a point p) where Serre duality fails.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The example shows h^1(X,O_X(-d)) need not vanish, contradicting Serre duality combined with Serre vanishing, hence CM hypotheses cannot be dropped wherever stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of Ext via locally free resolutions (Exercise 30.2.E)
rubrics_metrics.description: If 0 → ... → E_1 → E_0 → F → 0 is a resolution of F by locally free sheaves, then Ext^i(F, G) ≅ H^i(Hom(E^•, G)); thus Ext can be computed via finite-rank locally free resolutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is crucial: it lets one compute Ext by working affine-locally and using free resolutions. Consequence (Exercise 30.2.F): for coherent F,G on a quasi-projective scheme Ext^i_X(F,G) is coherent when such locally free resolutions exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local-to-global spectral sequence for Ext (Exercise 30.2.K)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a spectral sequence with E_2-term H^j(X, Ext^i(F,G)) abutting to Ext^{i+j}(F,G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct from the Grothendieck composition-of-functors spectral sequence once Hom(F,I) is shown Γ-acyclic for injective I (Exercise 30.2.J). This relates sheaf-Ext to global Ext groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Yoneda cup product and composition of Exts (30.2.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ext groups compose: there is a graded composition Ext^•(A,B) × Ext^•(B,C) → Ext^•(A,C) (30.2.3.2), and in O-module categories a natural product Hi(X,F) × Ext^j(F,G) → H^{i+j}(X,G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives the cup-product used in trace versions of duality; construction uses Hom complexes and injective resolutions, and yields associativity and module structures needed to define pairings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of π!_sh as right-adjoint to π_* for finite/affine morphisms (30.3.1–30.3.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an affine (in particular finite) morphism π: X → Y, define π!_sh G := π^{-1} Hom_Y(π_* O_X, G) (sheafified version) giving an adjoint pair (π_*, π!_sh) between QCoh_X and QCoh_Y (Ex. 30.3.A, 30.3.B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When π is finite and Y locally Noetherian, π!_sh sends coherent sheaves to coherent sheaves. For closed embeddings one can similarly define π!_sh on Mod; π!_sh preserves injectives in that context (Exercise 30.3.C). This functor is the sheaf-level analogue of Grothendieck's π!, used to transfer dualizing sheaves via finite maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite cover by P^n: existence of finite morphism to projective space (Proposition 30.3.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any projective k-scheme X of pure dimension n admits a finite morphism π: X → P^n (and if X is Cohen–Macaulay then π is flat).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction via projection from a linear subspace disjoint from X (or via Veronese embedding when k finite). This allows reducing duality on X to duality on P^n via π!_sh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pullback of dualizing sheaf via π!_sh preserves Serre duality for vector bundles when π is flat (Proposition 30.3.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is finite flat and functorial Serre duality for Ext holds for Y with dualizing sheaf ω_Y, then functorial Serre duality for vector bundles holds for X with dualizing sheaf π!_sh(ω_Y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof uses adjointness (π_*,π!_sh), the projection formula, and the hypothesis of functorial Serre duality for Ext on Y to identify H^{n−i}(X,F^∨ ⊗ π!_sh ω_Y) with H^i(X,F)^∨ for locally free F on X.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer of Hom-duality along finite maps without flatness (Proposition 30.3.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is finite and the trace version of Serre duality for Hom holds for Y with (ω_Y,t_Y), then functorial Serre duality for Hom holds for X with ω_X = π!_sh ω_Y (no flatness required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A commutative diagram using adjointness yields the trace for X from t_Y (diagram (30.3.11.1)); hence Hom-duality transfers along finite maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functorial Serre duality for Ext for Cohen–Macaulay projective schemes (Proposition 30.3.13 & Corollary 30.3.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is Cohen–Macaulay projective of pure dimension n and π: X → P^n is a finite flat morphism, then functorial Serre duality for Ext holds for X with dualizing sheaf ω_X := π!_sh(ω_{P^n}). Consequently, functorial Serre duality for Ext holds for all equidimensional Cohen–Macaulay projective k-schemes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof reduces to verifying both sides of Ext^i_X(·, π!_sh ω_{P^n}) ∼= H^{n−i}(X,·)^∨ are universal δ-functors and uses Serre vanishing plus projection formula and locally free properties of π_* O_X.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjunction formula and behaviour of dualizing sheaf under Cartier divisors (30.4 introduction)
rubrics_metrics.description: The dualizing sheaf behaves well with respect to slicing by effective Cartier divisors; one can describe the dualizing sheaf for a subvariety in terms of the dualizing sheaf of the ambient variety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is used to prove Desideratum 30.1.1 (that the canonical bundle is Serre-dualizing). Preliminary observations explain how Ext^i_{Y}(π_* O_X, G) acquires an O_X-module structure when π: X → Y is a closed embedding (30.4.1 and Exercise 30.4.A).
